name: Which pages should be included in a website audit for AI search if I have a huge website?

mainEntity.name: Which pages should be included in a website audit for AI search if I have a huge website?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Most businesses should audit their highest-value service pages first, then expand to supporting questions. A broad crawl is useful, but prioritization should follow revenue importance, customer confusion, local competition, and existing search demand.

Context: AI Visibility Solutions breaks broad services into specific scenarios, such as urgency, cost, suitability, preparation, and location. That approach is more useful than auditing every URL equally when a site has hundreds of pages.

Key factors:
- Pages tied to profitable or frequently requested services.
- URLs already receiving impressions but few clicks or inquiries.
- Pages with thin, outdated, duplicated, or difficult-to-extract answers.
- Local pages where service area and availability differ.

Practical guidance: Request a tiered audit: critical technical blockers, priority service pages, question gaps, and later improvements. For a limited budget, start with one service category and its most important customer questions.

AI Visibility Solutions can scope the review around the services most likely to produce qualified conversations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Audit revenue-critical service pages first, followed by pages already receiving impressions and pages answering common customer problems. Use a tiered plan: technical blockers, priority pages, question gaps, and lower-priority improvements.
